## Source: amazon-inspector (ec3d46c2bde8cb24c00a6d3fbf4efc912644488e11095244b75ac3f0f22df4d6)
On import of the MRCL2 package, __init__.py loads.core, which at module top level calls os.listdir('.') to enumerate the installer's current working directory and opens a TCP socket to the hardcoded host ejwdi-13-205-45-209.run.pinggy-free.link on port 40371, sending the directory listing to that endpoint. The destination is an ephemeral pinggy.link tunnel unrelated to the package's stated 'Document integrity utility' purpose, and the beacon fires on any import with no consent, no configuration, and no documented behavior. In CI and developer environments the working directory frequently contains sensitive project file names, making this an import-time reconnaissance exfiltration channel.

## Source: kam193 (9b2096354c3f06cc95c7258715128045f864fa7f05439e10caa7b7bf4e98ffc6)
During import, package exfiltrate listing of the current directory, and there is no other functionality. It is closely related to campaign 2026-11-my-poc-sandbox, which included a reverse shell.
